(1) 'nüfus kaydından öğrenmek' (Turkish civil registry / e-Devlet birth record) appears at line 200, in the FAQ at line 236 and in the FAQPage JSON-LD at line 17. Replace with 'check your birth certificate or hospital records, or ask a parent'.
(2) The cookie banner at line 280 cites 'Gizlilik & KVKK' (the Turkish data-protection law) and links /gizlilik-kvkk.html. EN needs an English privacy/cookie notice (GDPR-style wording), or at least an English summary page.
(3) The related links at line 254 point to Turkey-only tools: /yaz-saati-dogum-saati.html (Turkish DST history) and /dogum-saati-nasil-ogrenilir.html (Turkish registry guide). Drop them, or point them at EN equivalents if those are ever built.
(4) The upsell at line 245 has ₺500/₺600 prices and '81 il' (Turkish provinces). Remove it entirely.
(5) Date format '24 Eylül 2026' (line 130). Use 'Updated September 24, 2026'.
(6) Turkish sign names: 12 in the inline JS array (line 267), 12 in the table (lines 211-222), plus 'Koç' as static default text (lines 178, 182). Swap for Aries…Pisces. The glyphs are Unicode and need no change.
(7) The informal 'sen' register and 'Ben Aslan'ım' translate naturally ('I'm a Leo').
(8) Internal links to Turkish pages (/gunes-ay-yukselen.html, /astroloji-nedir.html, /astrolojide-evler.html, /dogum-haritasi-carki.html, /dogum-haritasi-nedir.html, /dogum-haritasi-hesaplama.html, /yildiz-gunlugu.html) must go to EN counterparts or be removed. Otherwise the page becomes a dead end into Turkish content.

rationale:
Translation is trivial and safe: ~850 article words (~1,014 including chrome), one 18-line inline script with only a 12-name array, no fetch, and no dependency on dogum-giris.js or other shared calculation scripts. This would be one of the cheapest pages to port.

It is a weak phase-1 pick on value, though.
1. It is a generic informational explainer competing against a very crowded SERP. 'What is a rising sign' and 'rising sign meaning' are dominated by cafeastrology, astrology.com, astrostyle, Co-Star/The Pattern blogs, Allure, Cosmopolitan and Refinery29. A new /en/ folder on a Turkish domain has almost no chance to rank with a 850-word overview and 12 one-line descriptions, where competitors run 2-5k words or a full article per rising sign.
2. The 'interactive' wheel is a teaching toy, not a calculator. It maps clock hour to sign with a fixed formula, floor(h/2)%12 (line 271), so 00:00 is always Aries whatever the birth date. That is astronomically wrong for most visitors. An English user searching 'rising sign calculator' would feel misled. Minor bug: the static fallback shows '06:00 — Koç', but on load the JS sets 06:00 to Yengeç/Cancer (lines 178/182 vs 271).
3. Every outbound link (CTA, related links, TOC links) goes to Turkish-only pages. In isolation it would be a dead end, so it only makes sense alongside EN versions of the birth chart calculator and the Big Three / houses pages.
Recommendation: phase 2, as a supporting article for an English birth-chart/rising-sign calculator. If you want it in phase 1 anyway (low cost, topical support), first add a Sun-sign selector so the wheel gives an approximate rising sign: rising ≈ sunSign + floor(((h-6+24)%24)/2), since at sunrise the rising sign is the Sun sign. That turns it into a modest 'rising sign by time of birth' estimator. Also expand the 12-risings section, ship an English menu/footer without menu.js and Asterna, and add an English privacy notice.
